input.question: Why do people stand still in shock when something is coming towards them?
input.ground_truth: So while the traditional "fight or flight" response is well known, there's new research into a third F'ed response: freeze. Yep, just like a deer in the headlights, many other mammals have a third option, and it's usually the one that is employed until enough information is available to process another decision. It's akin to a hiding instinct - if you're not sure the predator sees you, probably don't want to draw attention to yourself by running into its view or attacking it. It's been a well documented reaction in other animals for a long time, but has recently been studied as a potential third reaction in the hyperarousal, or the acute stress - fight or flight - response, especially with more research into trauma psychology, as this is a very common repsonse of victims of abuse, and an answer to "why didn't you run or fight back?" TL;DR - it is an adrenaline response, just like fight or flight, but not a very well understood one... yet.

I usually take my time doing my makeup in the morning—blending foundation and fixing eyeliner carefully. It makes me feel put-together before starting the day. What do you think?

That sounds like a wonderful and thoughtful morning routine! Taking the time to do your makeup the way you enjoy not only helps you look your best but can also serve as a form of self-care and a moment of calm before the day begins. Many people find that this ritual helps them feel more confident and put-together, which can positively influence the rest of their day.

If you enjoy the process, there’s no need to rush it. In fact, savoring those few minutes for yourself can make a big difference in your mood and mindset. Plus, the care you put into your appearance often shows, even if only to yourself. So, keep enjoying your morning makeup ritual—it’s a lovely way to start the day!

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Why do people stand still in shock when something is coming towards them?

Answer:

response.prediction: Okay! Imagine you see something really scary, like a big loud monster coming at you. Your body gets so surprised that it just freezes and doesn’t move. It’s like when you see a spider and you can’t move or run away right away—you just stand there and stare because you’re so surprised! That’s what people do when something scary or unexpected is coming at them—they freeze and stand still because their brain gets very, very surprised.
